subject: math
title: Mean
summary: The mean (average) is the total of all data points divided by how many there are. Explore the 'fair share' idea behind the mean and how to compute it.

compareCandidate.label: Mean vs. median
compareCandidate.description: The mean is the fair-share value computed from all points; the median is simply the middle point. An outlier can pull them far apart.

plainLanguageExplanation: The mean is the average — the value you get when you share all the data evenly. Add up every data point, then divide by how many points there are. If four friends collect 2, 4, 6, and 8 shells, the total is 20, and sharing evenly gives each friend 20 ÷ 4 = 5 shells. The mean is '5'. Because the mean uses every point, one huge or tiny value (an outlier) can pull the mean up or down a lot — that is why you sometimes prefer the median.

keyFacts.label: Formula
keyFacts.value: Sum of points ÷ number of points

keyFacts.label: Caution
keyFacts.value: Outliers can pull the mean strongly

whyItMatters: The mean is the world's most-used number — batting averages, test scores, temperatures, and salaries all lean on it. Knowing what it means (and when it lies) helps you read every headline that cites an 'average'.
didYouKnow: The word 'average' once meant the fee a ship owner paid to spread out damage to a cargo — the 'fair share' idea has been baked into averages for hundreds of years.
compareReason: Students think average and middle are the same — comparing the fair-share mean with the middle-point median shows the difference.
